notes.summary: All-ordinal generated-Psh cone operations and ordinary signed test measures in the full target scope; no continuous-recognition or universal multiplier claim.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves cone closure at every sheafified ordinal successor and limit, so finite continuous generated-Psh differences form a vector space. Constructs compact signed Radon measures for canonical curvature and ordinary multiplier tests using middle-positive decomposition, differential duality and retained generic lengths. Records all external premises with versioned primary evidence. These are foundations, not a solution of P21.3.
notes.text:
Foundations for the original-pair reduction; unverified research draft.

Retain the unchanged scope: K any complete non-Archimedean field, including trivial valuation; X good separated strict boundaryless pure n-dimensional, n>=2; W any ordinary open; T middle-positive ordinary CLD (p,p), 0<=p<=n-1, d'T=d''T=0. Put D=d'd'' and [f]=f delta_X, retaining actual generic Artinian component lengths.

Let P(W)=C(W) intersect generated CLD-Psh(W), where C(W) consists of finite real continuous functions. Then P(W) is a cone containing constants, and E(W)=P(W)-P(W)=span_R P(W) is a vector space. No Psh-to-CPsh recognition is needed.

Proof at every sheafified ordinal: rank zero is the smooth positive-Hessian cone. At a successor, choose decreasing representations for two sections near a point, intersect their two ordinary neighbourhoods, and restrict both sequences there. Their fixed nonnegative linear combination belongs to the preceding cone and decreases to the desired combination. Ordinary sheaf locality gives successor membership. Zero coefficients are omitted, avoiding undefined multiplication by minus infinity. Decreasing limits preserve upper semicontinuity because strict sublevel sets are unions of the predecessor sublevel sets. At a limit ordinal lambda, two sections locally have ranks xi,zeta<lambda; after intersecting neighbourhoods both lie in rank max(xi,zeta)<lambda. That rank's cone property and ordinary locality establish the limit case. Constants persist throughout.

The family stabilizes by considering the set of all pairs (ordinary open, ambient function section): it cannot add a new pair at every successor beyond that set's cardinal successor. Equality with a successor fixes all subsequent stages. The stationary sheaf contains the generators and is closed under decreasing sequences on each fixed open, hence is the minimal Psh sheaf. This argument needs no integrability qualification. Taking finite continuous sections preserves cone operations. Splitting signed coefficients then proves E=span_R P. This does not assert that arbitrary locally represented differences glue to a global difference.

For compact symmetric smooth beta of degree (n-1,n-1), define the canonical signed top-form measure lambda_beta by
integral f d lambda_beta=<D[f],beta>.
For compact symmetric smooth alpha of degree (n-p-1,n-p-1), define nu_(T,alpha) by
integral f d nu_(T,alpha)=<D(fT),alpha>.
Both are finite signed compact Radon measures. Their supports lie respectively in supp(beta) and supp(alpha).

To construct nu, decompose eta=D alpha as eta1-eta2 with compact middle-positive smooth eta_i. Middle positivity makes g -> <T,g eta_i> positive scalar Radon measures mu_i, with finite masses. Their difference evaluates continuous f through the ordinary order-zero product as <fT,D alpha>=<D(fT),alpha>. Different decompositions agree on smooth scalar tests and hence, by uniform smooth scalar density, on continuous tests; their signed measures coincide. Outside supp(eta), all smooth scalar pairings vanish. Density in that complementary open shows that the signed measure vanishes there. Thus its support lies in supp(eta), hence supp(alpha), even if the decomposition supports are larger. For lambda_beta use the canonical measure of D beta and the same differential duality. No tropical pushforward or replacement of delta_X by delta_Xred is involved.

Consequently, for a compact C containing the two decomposition supports,
|<D((f-g)T),alpha>| <= ||f-g||_C <T,eta1+eta2>.
This controls locally uniform nets for the original fixed current and test. It establishes convergence of differentiated products, not a vanishing limit for an unknown multiplier.

Complete external-premise list, with nonnegative indices:

Premise 0. Analytic spaces have compact-neighbourhood bases, and ordinary opens are analytic domains with canonical restricted structure (CLD 11.1.7). A topologically separated pure n-dimensional analytic space has the canonical calibrated CLD level-n calculus; analytic-domain calculus agrees with restriction (15.7.1–2). Integration over a pure closed analytic subspace equals integration over its associated cycle (16.6.3), retaining generic multiplicities. Applicability: the target and its ordinary opens have the required scope; delta_X is retained. Primary evidence, premise 0: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 14983–15012, 22105–22126 and 23434–23459.

Premise 1. CLD Definition 8.1.1 defines Psh as the smallest ordinary subsheaf of functions valued in R union {-infinity}, containing smooth positive-Hessian functions and closed under decreasing sequential limits. Lemma 8.1.4 uses ordinary-local decreasing limits at successors and ordinary-local earlier-rank membership at limits. Lemma 8.1.2 states the upper-semicontinuous cone property. Applicability: only finite continuous final sections are used; cone operations were reconstructed above without continuity of intermediate approximants. Primary evidence, premise 1: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 9729–9781.

Premise 2. CLD Proposition 6.5.2 expresses a compact symmetric smooth (q,q) test as a difference of two compact middle-positive tests within its support scope; that scope explicitly includes compact supports on almost-good analytic spaces. Definition 7.2.1 defines middle positivity by symmetry and nonnegative pairing against middle-positive complementary forms. Applicability: goodness suffices for the compact support condition. No spanning by strongly positive forms is used. Primary evidence, premise 2: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 7359–7381 and 7918–7981.

Premise 3. On locally differentially separated level-n spaces, positive scalar currents are positive Radon measures (CLD 7.2.8). Pairing a middle-positive current with a complementary middle-positive form gives its positive coefficient measure, with compact support for compact forms (7.2.11). Locally bounded Borel functions have the ordinary order-zero product, agreeing with smooth multiplication (7.2.12). Applicability: finite continuous functions are locally bounded. Only positive coefficient measures and their differences are used; the broad strongly-positive spanning inference in 7.2.9 is not imported. Primary evidence, premise 3: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 7983–8011, 8054–8076 and 7918–7981.

Premise 4. Ordinary forms have exterior products, differential Leibniz rules and compatible restriction (CLD 3.3.10–12). Ordinary currents restrict and form a sheaf (7.1.6–7). Their differential convention satisfies d'^2=d''^2=0, d''d'=-d'd'', DJ=JD, and <DS,alpha>=<S,D alpha> (7.7.1–5). Applicability: the identities and symmetric-test reduction are used on the actual ordinary W. Primary evidence, premise 4: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 3769–3803, 7756–7818 and 9309–9381.

Premise 5. Good Hausdorff analytic spaces are locally holomorphically and differentially separated. Compact sets inside opens have compact smooth cutoffs, and compact continuous scalars admit uniform smooth approximation within that open (CLD 15.2.2–7). Smooth compact top forms have canonical finite signed Radon measures and their scalar integration rule (5.8.1–6). Applicability: the target W satisfies these conditions for either valuation; no global paracompactness is added. Primary evidence, premise 5: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 21619–21696 and 6733–6808.

Premise 6. CPsh is the smallest ordinary continuous subsheaf containing smooth positive-Hessian functions and stable under uniform sequential limits (CLD Definition 8.1.7); Lemma 8.1.8 gives its sheafified ordinal stages. For smooth scalar f and symmetric doubly closed T, D(fT)=Df wedge T (8.5.3–4). Positive smooth factors preserve middle positivity (7.2.7). The actual proof of 8.5.5 establishes multiplier positivity for CPsh by minimality and uniform convergence. Applicability: used for the subsequent audit, without importing Proposition 8.1.11's reverse recognition. Primary evidence, premise 6: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2, inclusive UTF8 LF 9797–9863, 10287–10326 and 7918–7981.

Premise 7. GJR v3 assumes complete nontrivially valued K. On its good strict space scope, Proposition 10.17 equates weak smoothness with zero weak form-Hessian to GJR harmonicity, hence real PL. Section 7.13 instead defines its psh terminology by ordinary Hessian-current positivity. Sections 12.1–2 define strong currents on weakly smooth tests and their restriction to ordinary currents. Applicability: these are scope diagnostics only; no arbitrary-function recognition, closed positive lift or ordinary product compatibility is inferred. Primary evidence, premise 7: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.05741v3, inclusive UTF8 LF 339–343, 3185–3191, 3365–3386, 2529–2581 and 3618–3636.

Versions and source hashes: CLD arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, SHA256 64846cb00926267c6238d1afac61b5eaed0a0e3a6349725738f9b1bf163de085; GJR arXiv:2111.05741v3, 7 March 2025, SHA256 57dfcae1d8dfc25d5ef217f34fabe9e80b679ec2956db1bced3b31bc9afdf8d3. notes.summary: Exact original-pair dual reduction: pair-tested weak closure equals finite interpolation and signed curvature-relation preservation. Failure would produce actual Psh potentials, but neither failure nor universal closure is established.
notes.detailedSummary: For every fixed target W,T, proves equivalence of the continuous generated-Psh pair predicate, closure tested on Psh-continuous differences, exact finite interpolation on actual psh tuples, and preservation of signed curvature dependencies. Finite-dimensional separation produces two admissible potentials on the same analytic open. The criterion retains every target hypothesis but remains unverified for arbitrary singular currents; no analytic counterexample is constructed.
notes.text:
Exact dual criterion for the original finite continuous generated-Psh pair class; unverified research draft. This is a formal reduction, not a universal proof or a constructed analytic counterexample.

Use the unchanged scope, cone result and ordinary signed measures of n1. On W put P=Psh(W) intersect C(W), E=P-P=span_R P, H={h in C(W):D[h]=0}, and L={lambda_beta: beta compact smooth symmetric of degree (n-1,n-1)}. The map beta -> lambda_beta is linear, so L is a vector subspace without a positivity restriction. Give the compact signed Radon measures M_c(W) the weak topology sigma(M_c,E). Because E=span_R P, this is also the topology generated by evaluations against actual functions in P alone. Hausdorffness need not be assumed.

For fixed W,T, the original equal-curvature pair assertion is equivalent to each of these conditions:

(a) For every compact smooth symmetric alpha of degree (n-p-1,n-p-1), nu_(T,alpha) belongs to the sigma(M_c,E) closure of L.

(b) For every alpha and finite tuple u1,...,um in P, there exists one compact smooth symmetric beta of degree (n-1,n-1), depending on the tuple, such that <D[ui],beta>=<D(uiT),alpha> for every i.

(c) Every finite signed curvature relation sum ci D[ui]=0 among actual ui in P satisfies sum ci <D(uiT),alpha>=0 for every alpha.

Proof. By the defining measure formula and symmetry, H is exactly L's annihilator in C(W); E intersect H is its annihilator in E. These are precisely original equal-curvature pair differences: E consists of U-V with U,V actual finite continuous generated Psh, and D[U]=D[V] means D[U-V]=0. Under (a), evaluation against any such h vanishes on L, hence on its closure and every nu_(T,alpha). Therefore <D(hT),alpha>=0 for every symmetric alpha. Since T and hT are symmetric and DJ=JD, D(hT) is symmetric; antisymmetric tests also vanish. Thus D(hT)=0.

Conversely suppose an actual nu=nu_(T,alpha) is outside that closure. A basic weak neighbourhood avoiding L is described by finitely many actual u1,...,um in P and a positive tolerance. Define F(mu)=(integral ui d mu)_i in R^m. Its image S=F(L) is a vector subspace and is closed: extend its basis to a basis of R^m, making it the zero locus of the remaining linear coordinates. The missing neighbourhood implies F(nu) is outside S. Orthogonal projection onto S-perp supplies c=(ci) with c dot S=0 and c dot F(nu) nonzero. Set
U=sum max(ci,0) ui,
V=sum max(-ci,0) ui,
h=U-V.
The all-rank cone result of n1 makes U,V finite continuous generated Psh on the same W, without CPsh conversion. For every ordinary compact symmetric beta,
<D[h],beta>=c dot F(lambda_beta)=0.
Symmetry then gives D[h]=0 against all ordinary tests, hence the upstairs equation D[U]=D[V]. Yet
<D((U-V)T),alpha>=c dot F(nu) != 0.
Thus an exhibited failure of (a) would supply the required analytic potentials, current and compact smooth test, retaining the original field, analytic space, degree and generic lengths. No such failure is exhibited here.

For a fixed tuple define A(beta)=(<D[ui],beta>)_i and v=(<D(uiT),alpha>)_i. Its image S=A(tests)=F(L) has orthogonal complement consisting exactly of c with sum ci D[ui]=0, since all symmetric ordinary compact tests are available and the sum is symmetric. Condition (c) therefore says v annihilates S-perp, equivalently v belongs to S. This is precisely (b). Weak closure implies v belongs to the closure of S; finite-dimensional closedness upgrades approximation to exact interpolation. Conversely exact interpolation places a member of L in every finite-evaluation neighbourhood, proving (a). This proves all equivalences by finite-dimensional linear algebra, with no current-density premise.

When the criterion holds for fixed alpha, direct finite subsets F of P by inclusion and select beta_F interpolating F exactly. The net lambda_(beta_F) eventually agrees with nu on each prescribed Psh function and thus converges against E. No common compact support or uniform total-variation bound is asserted, and this is not approximation by positive closed currents. If the tuple curvatures D[ui] are linearly independent, S-perp=0 and interpolation is automatic for that tuple. Only exact signed dependencies can supply finite certificates. Their preservation for arbitrary singular currents remains unproved.

This refines the supplied all-continuous-kernel dual criterion. Since E is contained in C(W), closure in sigma(M_c,C(W)) is a sufficient stronger condition. Failure of that stronger closure can produce a continuous harmonic multiplier without producing a Psh pair. Failure of the pair-class closure above instead produces admissible Psh potentials by coefficient splitting. No equality of the closures or generation of arbitrary continuous functions by P is assumed.

Every-open quantification remains unchanged: for a global T, the equivalence must be applied independently on every ordinary W subset X. The proof extends no potentials from W, turns no cover into a basis, and assumes no sheaf gluing of globally represented differences. Trivial valuation and singular/nonreduced calibration are retained through the original ordinary products and canonical delta_X.

The indispensable unresolved statement is exact finite interpolation for every allowed K,X,p,T,W,alpha and every actual finite continuous generated-Psh tuple. Equivalently every signed curvature dependency must persist after multiplying by T. This note neither proves that universal condition nor gives an analytic tuple violating it. It adds no verified geometric range to the catalogue and does not solve P21.3.

The complete argument is Theorem 1 and Sections 3–5 of P21.3-paper.tex/P21.3-paper.pdf and P21.3-argument.md. Primary premises and evidence are stated in n1. Run `bash reproduce.sh` to regenerate the packet and check integrity and compilation. These execution checks do not certify the mathematics.

notes.detailedSummary: Audits base, successor and limit recognition steps, separating valid cone closure and CPsh inclusion from the missing reverse-recognition inference. Records the need for ordinary-local fixed-neighbourhood positive gluing and the actual CPsh scope of multiplier positivity. Topological and Euclidean diagnostics are not analytic counterexamples. notes.text:
Source audit and exact residual gap. Original P21.3 remains unresolved; this diagnostic is not evidence of a negative answer.

The primary CLD version is arXiv:1204.6277v2, 25 July 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.6277v2. Its supplied UTF8 text SHA256 is 64846cb00926267c6238d1afac61b5eaed0a0e3a6349725738f9b1bf163de085. LF indices mean raw bytes decoded UTF8 and split('\n'), inclusive one-based lines. Selected complete pertinent bodies were read, not the whole book. Literal statements and proofs, retaining extraction defects, are preserved in P21.3-primary-evidence.md and P21.3-argument.md. Hashes identify bytes rather than establish mathematical correctness.

Definition 8.1.1, LF 9729–9734, generates Psh as an ordinary sheaf using smooth positive-Hessian functions and decreasing sequential limits. Definition 8.1.7, LF 9797–9805, generates CPsh as a continuous ordinary sheaf using the smooth generators and uniform sequential limits. Proposition 8.1.11, LF 9835–9863, claims CPsh_xi=C intersect Psh_xi for every ordinal, but its successor proof changes the antecedent without providing a justification. Its pertinent literal text is:

"une fonction continue u définie sur un ouvert U est localement limite décroissante de
fonctions de CPshX,α si et seulement si elle est localement limite uniforme de telles
fonctions."

These are LF 9841–9843, followed at LF 9844 by:

"Soit U un ouvert de X et soit (un ) une suite décroissante de fonctions de CPshX,α (U )"

The required successor antecedent is a continuous limit of arbitrary Psh_xi sections, which can be discontinuous. The induction hypothesis identifies only continuous Psh_xi sections with CPsh_xi. It does not identify the arbitrary predecessor approximants. The printed Dini argument consequently handles continuous approximants after assuming them; it does not supply them. This is a gap in the quoted proof, not a counterexample to the recognition theorem.

The ordinal audit is precise. The base rank is valid. At a limit, recognition follows locally from recognition at every earlier rank: a continuous section locally belonging to an earlier Psh rank can locally use its corresponding CPsh rank, followed by CPsh sheaf locality. No single global earlier rank is needed. Every successor still requires replacement of possibly discontinuous predecessor approximants, including the ordinary covers introduced in their sheaves. The operation proof in n1 works at all ranks but establishes cone closure, not rank collapse.

Compact upper selection alone cannot provide that replacement. If upper-semicontinuous uj decrease to continuous finite u, the increasing open sets {uj-u<epsilon} cover any compact C. A finite subcover gives one j with u<=uj<u+epsilon on C. This holds with discontinuous uj but does not make them CPsh. For a purely topological diagnostic, on [0,1] take fj=(1/j) times the indicator of {0}. Each fj is upper semicontinuous, discontinuous and decreasing; the limit is continuous zero and convergence is uniform. These are not claimed to be analytic Psh functions.

Intermediate ordinary sheafification supplies variable representation neighbourhoods and covers. Fixed-domain transfinite selection omitting that sheafification does not glue local smooth leaves into one positive-Hessian approximant on a common ordinary neighbourhood. An infinite intersection of shrinking neighbourhoods need not contain a neighbourhood. At a limit, finitely many patches admit a maximum earlier rank but still require an actual positive gluing construction. Partitions of unity do not automatically preserve Hessian positivity: on (0,1), convex smooth x and 0 combined with positive weights 1-x and x yield x-x^2, with second derivative -2. This diagnoses that operation and is not an analytic counterexample. Other positive gluing methods are not ruled out.

The safe inclusion CPsh subset C intersect Psh is independently justified. For finite Psh fj converging uniformly to continuous f, set ej=||fj-f||. If infinitely many errors vanish, use that subsequence. Otherwise choose a subsequence with successive errors less than one-third the preceding error. Then fj+2ej decreases along that subsequence to f. Constants and the Psh cone give membership of the shifted functions. Thus the continuous part of Psh is a uniform-closed sheaf containing the generators and contains CPsh. This proves no reverse recognition.

The actual proof of CLD 8.5.5, LF 10317–10326, considers the continuous sheaf of f for which D(fT) is positive, includes smooth generators by the smooth multiplier identity, and uses uniform-product continuity. Its final literal phrase at LF 10326 is:

"contient le faisceau CPshX , ce qu’il fallait démontrer."

This is a valid CPsh multiplier-positivity proof using the ordinary measure and positive-factor facts in n1. Applying it to all continuous generated Psh needs the reverse recognition step. Both h and -h in CPsh suffice for BT: both signs of D(hT) are positive, and compact positive-test decomposition plus symmetry forces zero. Recognizing U,V individually as CPsh does not itself give both signs of U-V. No subtraction preserving the cone or approximation preserving their equal-curvature identity has been supplied.

GJR v3, 7 March 2025, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2111.05741v3, has text SHA256 57dfcae1d8dfc25d5ef217f34fabe9e80b679ec2956db1bced3b31bc9afdf8d3. LF 339–343 require nontrivial valuation. Section 7.13, LF 2529 onward, defines its psh terminology by current positivity rather than generated CLD-Psh. Proposition 10.17, LF 3367–3386, begins with weak smoothness and zero weak form-Hessian, not an arbitrary continuous ordinary-zero-current function. Sections 12.1–2, LF 3618–3636, define strong-current restriction without providing both a closed positive lift and ordinary multiplier compatibility. Neither is assumed here. The task-granted strict real-PL theorem is retained only within its supplied scope; the missing new recognition is for arbitrary original pair differences. Curve function recognition does not restrict a higher-dimensional ambient current equation to a curve.

The exact unresolved universal assertion from n2 is: for every allowed field, space, current, ordinary W, compact symmetric alpha, and finite continuous generated-Psh tuple ui, every relation sum ci D[ui]=0 must imply sum ci <D(uiT),alpha>=0. Equivalently the tuple's multiplier values must admit exact interpolation by an actual compact ordinary beta. No proof for all singular currents and no analytic tuple/current/test violating this condition has been supplied. The catalogue's known polycylinder, curve, real-PL, tower, invariant-toric and explicitly conditional approximation ranges are not counted as solutions. Generic lengths are retained; no coarse tropical pushforward decides the upstairs equation.
